_label: Evidence archive: Art Market Reform, 'WTF is Art' and Metaconceptual Art on Facebook and USA Projects (2012-2013)

identified_by.content: Evidence archive: Art Market Reform, 'WTF is Art' and Metaconceptual Art on Facebook and USA Projects (2012-2013)

content: Dated statements by the studio principal on Facebook in 2012 and 2013, with the times Facebook assigned them, and a public fundraising page he placed on the USA Projects site in 2013, captured by the Internet Archive. In public comments on posts by a New York art critic he wrote 'Coming Soon: Art Market Reform ! ! !' on 2012-08-14 at 05:20:21 UTC; 'Only thing better than that, would be open source, free, participatory, interactive, multi-media 21st century MetaConceptual Art, which wouldn't cost a dime, and could be open and available for the planet Earth 24/7/365, just like McDonalds' on 2012-11-16 at 07:25:18 UTC; '" Art Market Reform " sounds like profanity to many here among us' on 2012-11-21 at 12:50:29 UTC; and '#WTF is #Art ?! give thanks !' on 2012-11-21 at 14:34:42 UTC. In private messages he wrote on 2012-11-25 that he had started a Facebook page one or two days earlier, and that 'Art Historians from the Future is a simple example' of starting with analog art and changing it digitally; on 2013-05-29 that 'One of my more recent works of Metaconceptual Art is titled "Art Market Reform"'; and on 2013-07-23 that 'I am the creator of Metaconceptual Art and this is a Meta Art Work', of a work called 'The Art Market Bubble', closing with 'For the Love of God ... We are the Art.' The USA Projects page, 'Pittsburgh: City of Bridges, City of God', credited to Sun and Rain Works and captured on 2013-08-12, asks for support 'in the tradition of Metaconceptual Art' and gives its author's biography as 'I am a contemporary American metaconceptual Artist.' Together they carry several of the collection's titles and phrases earlier than any date this collection had held for them.

referred_to_by.content: What is earlier than before, and by how much. The public comment of 2012-08-14 is the earliest dated use of the title 'Art Market Reform' held here, thirteen months before the museum letter of 2013-09-12 that had been the earliest; the private message of 2013-05-29 is the earliest calling it a work of Metaconceptual Art. The comment of 2012-11-21 is the earliest dated appearance of the phrase 'WTF is Art' with a third party's date, nine months before the X post of 2013-08-29, and one day before the public posting of 2012-11-22 headed '#WTF is MetaConceptual Art ?!'. It was written on the day the registrar's receipts show ARTMARKETREFORM.ORG being registered, and a few hours after the comment that calls Art Market Reform profanity. The message of 2012-11-25 is the earliest dated naming of 'Art Historians from the Future', six months before the Flickr posting of the digital work on 2013-06-02. The USA Projects page is the earliest Internet Archive capture held here of a page carrying the term Metaconceptual Art of the studio's own work, on a site the studio did not run; it precedes the museum letter by a month. The public use of the term itself is older, in the posting of 2011-11-28. A further public comment, of 2012-08-14 at 23:04:51 UTC, on a post by an American writer and digital-rights campaigner, reads 'What Art Market Bubble ?'. It was written some eighteen hours after 'Coming Soon: Art Market Reform ! ! !', and it is the earliest dated use held here, in the studio principal's own words, of the phrase that names the work 'The Art Market Bubble', which the message of 2013-07-23 calls a Meta Art Work; it precedes by nine months the four ARTMARKETBUBBLE names the registrar's receipts show being registered on 2013-05-23. The question recurs in a comment of 2017-11-14, 'what art market bubble ?', on a public art page's post. The phrase itself is older in the studio's material, as a quotation rather than its own words: the WTFIA compilation 'IsItArt.doc', last saved on 2009-01-28 by its own metadata, includes a Financial Times report of 16 November 2008 headlined 'Recession woes pop art market bubble', as the record of the WTFIA folder sets out.

A message of 30 October 2012, before the definition was published. On 2012-10-30 at 15:18:13 UTC, by Facebook's clock, the studio principal wrote privately to an artist in New York whom he did not know; there was no reply: 'I had a profound to the core earth shattering "Art Vision" 4+ years ago, which illuminated to me the multidimensional nature of art. This was the birth of metaconceptual Art. Metaconceptual art has 8 defining characteristics, blah blah blah, its interconnected with the fabric of the Universe and it involves an interdisciplinary collaborative unification of our synergistic efforts to create the organic machinery of Living Art for the benefit of body mind and spirit of all human kind. For The Love of God, We Are the Art.' Three things in it are earlier than this collection had held. It refers to the eight defining characteristics twenty-three days before the public posting of 2012-11-22 that sets them out, though it does not list them. It is the earliest dated appearance of the line 'For the Love of God, We Are the Art', which the collection had otherwise first in a message of 2013-07-23 and in the website capture of 2014-12-18. And it places the 'Art Vision' that was 'the birth of metaconceptual Art' about four years before October 2012, that is in about 2008, where the studio's undated profile biography gives 2007. The recipient is not named. The thread's file in the account data, 2,333 bytes, has SHA-256 4f5d17de6efc3bf220792cf962eabfe7db80a70f941d6e427bd71abb05602f12, within the archive facebook-joechirum-2026-09-24-TZ87gGfq.zip, SHA-256 c978c3bd338a6a9a934d3aa05a81d2c298c49200bf7e4edc98b8329c02103097.

Evidence status. The Facebook items are dated by Facebook, from the account data it compiled and delivered on request on 2026-09-24, held by the studio as facebook-joechirum-2026-09-24-TZ87gGfq.zip, SHA-256 c978c3bd338a6a9a934d3aa05a81d2c298c49200bf7e4edc98b8329c02103097. The four comments are in the export's comments file, 874,950 bytes, SHA-256 6bccd7fe8c5e3057c9fccbdcffa62519501e3e8c3585eaccd09eb914ca5249d0. The messages are in three archived threads, of 88,494, 1,200 and 4,062 bytes, with SHA-256 1d3b2a20d85b4ac622e22750db44b1e758e777a65fe505577f9f5b95a0695993, 279fa2963258dd639e10907d1f4a0918ede159891b1bd2e227ab0a425aee980e and 3c39b34bdd158d8171c26ff9eef29eff1dc19f3122023bed5fd807b588f22def. The USA Projects page is dated by the Internet Archive, which captured it at 2013-08-12 08:16:17 UTC and again on 2013-08-14, with its supporting pages on 2013-09-17, at https://web.archive.org/web/20130812081617/http://www.usaprojects.org:80/project/pittsburgh_city_of_bridges_city_of_god. The capture as retrieved on 2026-09-24, 36,818 bytes, has SHA-256 a956b435d0b40f5522bdb73a20919ba2028f14e458e02c014ffbac741f723372. USA Projects was the fundraising programme of the non-profit United States Artists; the page shows a goal of $2,500, $50 raised, and a closing date of 21 August.

The studio principal's own profile page on the same site, not previously described here. The Internet Archive captured usaprojects.org/user/josephchirum on 2013-08-14 09:28:43 UTC and again on 2013-08-21 09:14:56 UTC; the captures as retrieved on 2026-09-28, 44,712 and 44,615 bytes, have SHA-256 d619f7b73d7cd7264a88156d2560e48878d6b2b6f961dd4515039bf838868a3f and b7e7cbc0074bcc685b8bab94d771eebd11291cd186863a80c51e20a35720e021. The page carries the same biography already held on the studio's Flickr, Tumblr and LinkedIn profiles, as far as it runs: Pittsburgh, the Philosophy and Religious Studies degrees, the move to Eugene, and the 2007 Art Vision, in the same words. It stops there. Neither capture continues to the sentence naming the 2009 Sotheby's sale that the fuller versions of this biography carry elsewhere; this page does not attach the term to that sale. The photograph on the page is credited 'self-portrait', copyright 2012. An 'External Links' section on the page points to 'The Art World is Flat' and '8 Sentences on Metaconceptual Art', both already held in this collection, showing this profile linked to them by August 2013.

Who the account followed, dated 2013-09-17. The profile's 'recent_connections' sub-page, captured 2013-09-17 00:12:08 UTC (retrieved 2026-09-28, 22,303 bytes, SHA-256 2905b3cd239d4cc815c10647d562a33abaf51a7b94ee774527101f6c583621c4), lists ten organisations and one individual the account followed on the platform, each with a count of other community members who had liked it: David Brin; Franklin Furnace Archive Inc. (27); the Ford Foundation (47); Creative Capital (63); CEC ArtsLink (24); the Alpert Award in the Arts (13); Artadia: The Fund for Art & Dialogue (26); Bloomberg Philanthropies (33); ArtSlant (15); and the Andy Warhol Foundation for the Visual Arts (65). The 'activity' sub-page, captured the same minute, gives the account's total as 19 organisations followed; only these ten are named on the pages held. All ten are real, named, public organisations or a public individual, and are recorded on that basis; none of this evidences any relationship between the studio and any of them beyond the act of following. The Warhol Foundation's presence on this list is noted without further weight; it joins, and does not by itself strengthen, the collection's separate account of the Business Art book photographed with the print in 2008.

The project's own updates page, carrying a fuller statement than the project page's tagline. Captured 2013-09-17 15:40:18 UTC (retrieved 2026-09-28, 16,986 bytes, SHA-256 cad339dffc7e70b3038c3cff7b395e5073482c84b3efd8d36b1d82c4fee7ae0d), the page carries a statement in the studio principal's own words, longer than the project page's own tagline already quoted in this record: that the project's goal is 'to bridge together The Art historical traditions of the past, with contemporary Art of the present, and the direction of Art into the Future, through the creation of Art'; that its aim is pencil, charcoal, oil pastel, acrylic and oil depictions of 'historical Pittsburgh landmarks, bridges, churches, sacred architecture, and every day scenes'; and that support is sought for art supplies, transport and studio rental, 'in the tradition of Metaconceptual Art', closing 'Thank You, Joseph M. Chirum'. It does not name the 2009 sale.

The project's one recorded backer. The project's 'supporters' sub-page, captured 2013-09-17 14:35:52 UTC (retrieved 2026-09-28, 12,748 bytes, SHA-256 2950bc7450c75d8bfb8b899826102b81f2dabe14e6207e158190d62896773dc6), names one backer, a community member of the platform based in Los Angeles, California, who pledged on 16 July 2013 and is shown as supporting 29 other projects there; the page states this is the only supporter, matching the '$50 of $2,500' shown on the project page itself. Following this collection's convention for private individuals, the backer is identified here by role and location only; their name, given on the page, is not published. This is the only third party found, in any of the pages checked, taking any action in relation to the project beyond a platform 'like'.

What these do and do not show. Every item is the studio principal's own writing; the Facebook dates and the archive's capture fix when he wrote or published it, not whether what he wrote is true. None of them concerns the 2009 sale, and none evidences the 2007 origin asserted elsewhere. The comments were made on a public figure's posts, where they could be read by others; the messages were private, and the page was public. That a phrase or title was in use by a date is all they establish, and each is recorded here for that. The later comments on the same critic's posts, 2013 to 2018. The four comments quoted above are not the whole series. The comments file holds twenty-three comments by the studio principal on the same New York art critic's public posts and photographs, from 2012-08-14 to 2018-12-02, at times Facebook assigns. Those of 2013 onward that concern the art market or the studio's titles are these: 'just as long as theres no difference between "insider money" and "outsider money" art=money #notrocketscience' (2013-02-10 16:26:00 UTC); 'must be time for #ArtMarketReform' (2013-05-25 04:25:01 UTC); 'time for "Art Market Reform"' (2014-02-06 18:11:12 UTC); 'Add some lovely anonymous buyers and sellers, a dash of insider trading, a teaspoon of market manipulation, a generous sprinkle of front running, money laundering to taste, and a generous helping of tax evasion. Another beautiful day in the Art World.' (2014-05-09 22:03:35 UTC); 'Art ... From the Top Down... Sounds like the end of civilization as we know it. Time for Art Market Reform. Multinational corporate money and sponsorship is not a requirement for great Art. What Hedge Funds ?!' (2015-07-30 01:10:38 UTC); 'Which candidate supports #ArtMarketReform ?!' (2016-06-22 22:06:32 UTC); 'Metaconceptual Art ?!' (2016-10-23 20:38:03 UTC); 'Spectacular theatrical market manipulation ! Bravo Ladies and Gentlemen' (2018-10-09 15:09:53 UTC); and 'Anyone in the Art world want to volunteer to start paying sales tax ?' (2018-10-18 22:36:06 UTC). The others are a question about an installation at the Hirshhorn Museum (2013-10-07), a sticker with no text (2015-07-30), and four remarks of 2018 on unrelated subjects or about the critic. None of these is earlier than an item already held for the same title or phrase. What they add is continuity: 'Art Market Reform' is in public use under the studio principal's name in every year from 2012 to 2016, and 'What Hedge Funds ?!' and 'Metaconceptual Art' recur alongside it. The comment of 2018-10-09 was written four days after the Banksy painting was shredded in Sotheby's London saleroom on 2018-10-05, and two days before the comments of 2018-10-11 set out in the record of the 2018 comments. The export does not preserve the photograph it answered, so what it refers to is not established, and this record does not say that it concerns that event. As with the comments above, only the studio principal's words are quoted, the critic is identified by role only, and the source is the same comments file, with the checksum given in the evidence-status note.

Privacy. The art critic whose posts carried the comments, and the writer on whose post the comment of 2012-08-14 about an art market bubble was made, are identified by role only, and the private correspondents are not named; nothing any of them wrote is reproduced. Only the studio principal's words are quoted. The Facebook page named in the message of 2013-05-29, facebook.com/ArtMarketReform, and the page the message of 2012-11-25 describes as newly started are not held, and the Internet Archive holds no capture of either from those years.
